summary: Literary and media production workshops, introduced in fall 2023, are spreading through schools worldwide, letting students turn written work into films, podcasts, documentaries and other media. The note profiles programs in Wellington, Tokyo, Parkside, London, Sydney and New York, showing benefits such as multiple literacies, global awareness, community engagement, social awareness, career readiness and interdisciplinary learning.
one_line: Since fall 2023, school workshops blending literature and media production have spread worldwide, building literacy, creativity, community engagement and career skills.
key_facts: Julia Marquez, an English teacher at Wellington High School, pioneered the first workshop on September 15th, 2023, blending written word with digital storytelling.
Wellington High students create short films, podcasts, and digital storyboards that accompany their essays and creative writing.

Kenji Sato of Shinjuku Secondary School in Tokyo introduced a cross-cultural literary exchange program on October 3rd, 2023, in which students worldwide write stories and adapt them into web series and interactive eBooks.
On November 8th, 2023, Parkside Middle School students led by media instructor Scott Reeves researched local folklore and turned it into documentaries.
The 'Voices From The Margins' workshop at Grandview School for Girls in London, led by Ayesha Philips, began on October 22nd, 2023.
In 'Voices From The Margins', students work with underrepresented community members to write and produce short films about their stories.
The Storytellers' Institute at Harborside Secondary in Sydney, founded by Lewis Carter, began on September 20th, 2023, and teaches students to pitch stories to media establishments and publishers.
Storytellers' Institute students have won writing contests, secured internships with media companies, and published their works.
At Lincoln Tech Academy in New York, science teacher Elijah Grant and English teacher Sandra Thompson started a joint program in the 2023-2024 academic year.
Lincoln Tech students write informative essays on scientific topics and convert them into podcasts or video essays.
Marquez says students live in a media-saturated world and must learn to produce their own narratives, not just consume content critically.
The note frames the workshops as a response to evolving information consumption and creation, redefining literacy in the 21st century.
